requirement: Describe an individually randomized two-arm parallel efficacy trial in low-income Black/African-American or Hispanic adults aged at least 65 years with type 2 diabetes and screening HbA1c at least 8%, comparing HOME DM-BAT with an attention-matched GHE/ST control.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the target population, randomized efficacy objective and both behavioral conditions.

requirement: Reconcile the control-condition description before freezing analysis labels: the protocol calls it GHE plus supportive therapy and says GHE matches diabetes education, but later says the control will not receive diabetes education.

evidence.text: The control paragraph both says GHE matches diabetes education and says the control will not receive diabetes education.

requirement: Specify 1:1 permuted-block randomization with varied undisclosed block sizes and stratification by baseline HbA1c 8-10% versus greater than 10%; separately document sequence generation, concealment and assignment implementation, which are not supplied.

evidence.text: The randomization paragraph defines the method and HbA1c strata but not operational concealment.

requirement: Define who is blinded or masked, how outcome assessment is protected from treatment knowledge and how unblinding is handled; varied block sizes alone do not establish participant, provider or assessor masking.

evidence.text: The protocol mentions maintaining the blind and hiding block size but does not assign masking roles.

requirement: Use assessments at baseline and 3, 6, 9 and 12 months after randomization, with 12 months as the primary efficacy timepoint; represent the eight weekly intervention sessions and ten monthly booster contacts without inventing additional efficacy visits.

evidence.text: The study overview gives the session schedule, follow-up visits and primary 12-month analysis.

requirement: Define the primary endpoint as glycemic control measured by HbA1c at 12 months and the primary contrast as the difference between HOME DM-BAT and GHE/ST in 12-month outcome means, with lower HbA1c favorable.

evidence.text: The aim and study overview designate HbA1c and the 12-month group comparison.
The plan confirms HbA1c and 12 months as the primary outcome and timepoint.

requirement: Predefine HbA1c units, laboratory source, acceptable measurement window, duplicate or out-of-range handling, baseline definition and whether the modeled endpoint is the observed value or change from baseline.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies HbA1c eligibility and efficacy use but omits executable derivation rules.

requirement: Use all randomized participants in the primary intention-to-treat analysis and attribute them to randomized HOME DM-BAT or GHE/ST regardless of adherence; distinguish the prospective 200-person ITT target from any later actual enrollment.

evidence.text: The plan states that primary analyses use the ITT set.
The protocol targets 200 participants randomized equally and inflates for ITT dilution and missingness.

requirement: Define a treatment-policy estimand for the 12-month HbA1c difference and state handling of intervention discontinuation, missed sessions or boosters, diabetes-medication changes, withdrawal, death and other intercurrent events.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomized longitudinal treatment but no intercurrent-event strategy.
The terse ITT statement does not define an estimand.

requirement: Implement the planned longitudinal mixed-effects framework with fixed effects for randomized treatment, visit and treatment-by-visit interaction and adjustment for baseline HbA1c stratum or value; prespecify participant random effects or residual covariance, degrees-of-freedom method and the 12-month contrast.

evidence.text: The reference specifies only a longitudinal mixed-effects framework for individual and correlated multiple outcomes.
The protocol supplies repeated timepoints and the HbA1c randomization stratum needed for a complete model.

requirement: Do not choose adjustment covariates after testing baseline imbalance. Prespecify whether race/ethnicity, sex, age, social support, health literacy, concurrent illness, depression and motivation enter the primary model, and retain the randomization stratum regardless of observed imbalance.

evidence.text: The reference proposes comparing baseline values for imbalance to identify potential confounders and lists candidate variables, leaving a data-dependent selection risk.

requirement: Report the adjusted 12-month between-arm HbA1c mean difference with a two-sided 95% confidence interval and p-value at alpha 0.05, plus model-based estimates by arm and visit; do not define success from significance alone without effect direction and magnitude.

evidence.text: The protocol states a directional superiority hypothesis and two-sided alpha 0.05 for power.
The plan refers to magnitude and significance of outcome-mean differences but omits confidence-interval reporting.

requirement: Specify how the mixed model handles intermittent and monotone missing HbA1c under an explicit missing-at-random assumption, which variables inform that assumption, and how participants lacking 12-month or all postbaseline measurements contribute.

evidence.text: The power calculation anticipates 20% missing information but gives no analysis rule.
The mixed-effects statement does not describe missing data.

requirement: Add a prespecified sensitivity analysis for departures from missing at random, such as reference-based or delta-adjusted multiple imputation, and a clearly labeled adherence-based supplementary analysis without replacing the ITT primary result.

evidence.text: The year-long intervention anticipates attrition and inflates sample size, but no robustness analysis is defined.

requirement: Protect the single HbA1c comparison at 12 months as primary and label other visits and unspecified correlated outcomes exploratory unless a prespecified secondary hierarchy and multiplicity method are supplied.

evidence.text: The protocol names one aim and 12-month primary analysis while collecting earlier visits.
The plan mentions correlated multiple outcomes without naming or ordering them.

requirement: State the prospective target of 200 randomized participants, 100 per arm, derived from 80 per arm for 85% power to detect a standardized HbA1c effect of 0.34-0.39 at two-sided alpha 0.05 and inflated by 20% for missing information and ITT dilution.

evidence.text: The sample-size paragraph supplies target, allocation, power, standardized effect, alpha and inflation.

requirement: Define the safety population and summarize adverse events and serious adverse events by randomized arm, severity, seriousness and relatedness, while separately reporting depression or suicidality triggers, venipuncture events and urgent blood-pressure findings.

evidence.text: The human-subjects and monitoring sections identify risks and DSMC/IRB adverse-event oversight but no statistical safety set or summaries.

requirement: List every intended nonprimary clinical, behavioral and psychosocial outcome with instrument, scoring, visit, direction and analysis status before modeling them; the reference phrase 'individual and correlated multiple outcomes' is not an executable endpoint specification.

evidence.text: The plan invokes individual and correlated multiple outcomes without identifying them.
The protocol discusses several behavioral, psychosocial and physiologic constructs without a formal endpoint table.

requirement: Expose rather than invent the unresolved control content, masking roles, mixed-model covariance and contrast, estimand, missing-data strategy, secondary endpoint inventory, multiplicity and detailed safety analysis.

evidence.text: The two-page reference supplies only a short analysis paragraph and leaves central executable decisions unspecified.

requirement: Keep the independent two-page Analysis Plan annotation-only and require original IRB or grant provenance confirming that both 2021-06-02 documents were outcome-uninformed before the 2025-06-30 primary completion; exclude the family if the post-completion uploads were retrospectively altered.

evidence.text: The protocol cover gives exact title, NCT and 2021-06-02 date.
The independent plan has the same identity/date and contains the reference-only mixed-effects method; registry records show both files were uploaded after completion.
